operations.specification: Register a new user account in the 'users' table. Requires role assignment, unique username, and unique email. Password must be provided (hashed on storage) and is never returned by API. Strict validation applies to all fields, enforcing business rules found in the users and user_roles Prisma models. Audit fields are written automatically by backend. Security validation ensures only self-registration or privileged roles can create users.
operations.description: This operation allows either new users to self-register (signup) or administrative users to create new user accounts. Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. Role assignment references the user_roles table (role name or ID). On successful creation, returns full non-sensitive account data (never returns password hash or plain password). Validation includes strong password policies, correctly-formed emails, unique username check, assignment of allowed roles, and correct audit metadata. Security policies ensure only authorized clients can create moderator/administrator accounts. Relationship: users references user_roles via user_role_id (UUID). The operation complements authentication endpoints and supports user onboarding workflows. Error handling includes duplicate entries, invalid roles, and input format errors.

operations.specification: Creates a new discussion post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a new record into the 'posts' Prisma table, enabling a user to start a thread on a relevant topic or question. Creating a post requires a category assignment and sufficient content to meet system validation rules.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.specification: Searches or lists comments attached to a specific post in the BBS platform, with support for filtering, pagination, and sorting. This operation targets the 'comments' Prisma table, enabling users and visitors to explore threads and reply-chains belonging to a post.
operations.description:
This API allows users to retrieve a list of comments for a specific post, identified by 'postId'. Supports query options for filtering by author, time range, reply depth, and more—including pagination and sort order. The underlying 'comments' table returns summaries or basics details of each comment thread or reply chain, supporting threaded conversation navigation.

Both authenticated users and visitors can access this operation, but may see different levels of detail according to permissions. The endpoint is closely linked with comment creation (POST), update (PUT), and deletion (DELETE) for participation and moderation flows. Only comments belonging to the target postId are returned, supporting thread-based exploration and analysis.

operations.specification: Creates a new comment in response to a specific post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a comment record in the 'comments' Prisma table, enabling users to participate in ongoing discussions, reply to threads, and contribute nested or direct responses. Parent-child threading is supported for reply chains.
operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

operations.specification: Implements the delete operation for a nested comment resource under a specific post. This endpoint enables an authorized user (such as the comment's author or a moderator) to delete a specific comment belonging to a post. The operation checks that the comment is indeed a direct child of the specified post. The underlying table is 'comments', and enforcement of proper soft-delete logic and audit trail is referenced from schema comments. Authorization must ensure that only legitimate actors can perform this action. Error handling is required if either the post or comment does not exist or the relationship is invalid.
operations.description:
This operation deletes a comment associated with a particular post in the political/economic discussion board application. According to the Prisma schema for the 'comments' table, deleting a comment does not remove the record from the database, but marks it as deleted by updating the 'deleted_at' timestamp. This is in line with moderation and audit requirements described in both the requirement analysis and schema documentation.

Authorization is necessary, and only the comment's author, a moderator, or an administrator may perform this action. Permissions are determined by checking the user's role, which is represented in the 'users' and 'user_roles' tables. The endpoint ensures that the specified comment exists, is associated with the given post, and is not already deleted. Attempting to delete a non-existent or unrelated comment results in an error response showing the appropriate message.

Additionally, the operation maintains an audit trail by recording the timestamp of deletion, as outlined in the comments schema. The deleted comment remains for future moderation or review, and cannot be interacted with by regular members after deletion. Error responses must comply with API design for invalid IDs, unauthorized access, and logical violations (such as trying to delete an already deleted comment).

By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.

event.review:
The draft follows best practices for negative scenario testing in an E2E test:
- It generates a UUID that is exceedingly unlikely to exist to ensure test isolation (avoiding accidental deletion of a real record).
- It attempts the deletion through the correct endpoint (eraseById).
- It uses TestValidator.error to assert that an error should be thrown, adhering to guidelines against error message validation or illegal TypeScript pattern usage.
- It stays within the API/DTO boundaries and does not use unapproved helpers or types.
- No attempt at TypeScript type system violations is made (all types are safe).

Edge Case: Even if by coincidence the generated UUID exists, in repeatable E2E environments such UUID collisions are almost impossible. If collision is a concern, a second attempt with a new UUID could be considered, but is not required unless instructed.

Conclusion: This code fully satisfies correctness, domain, and quality requirements for a negative deletion scenario.

- The test correctly overrides the connection headers to simulate no authentication.

The function follows all requirements for type safety, proper connection usage, appropriate error assertion, and documentation for why each step is taken.

Conclusion: The draft meets all requirements and should be moved to final code with any optional notes clarified for future test expansion if dependencies grow.

- **Scenarios Covered**: Both a malformed (not-a-uuid) and a well-formed, non-existent UUID are tested for the delete role endpoint.

- **Not Checking No Unrelated Deletion**: Point 3 in the scenario draft (about verifying no unrelated roles are deleted) cannot be implemented as the available SDK does not provide a list/query endpoint for roles. Skipping this is correctly noted.
- **Hardcoded Non-existent UUID**: The non-existent UUID used is arbitrary, no check is possible, but this is an industry-accepted practice for such error-path tests.
- **No Success Scenario Needed**: Since the scenario focuses on failure/validation, there is no need to set up or clean up test user roles.

#### Recommendations:
- No further enhancements needed for this scenario; implementation and style conform fully to requirements and typical E2E test conventions.

operations.specification: Register a new user account in the 'users' table. Requires role assignment, unique username, and unique email. operations.description: This operation allows either new users to self-register (signup) or administrative users to create new user accounts. Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. Role assignment references the user_roles table (role name or ID). On successful creation, returns full non-sensitive account data (never returns password hash or plain password). Validation includes strong password policies, correctly-formed emails, unique username check, assignment of allowed roles, and correct audit metadata. Security policies ensure only authorized clients can create moderator/administrator accounts. Relationship: users references user_roles via user_role_id (UUID). The operation complements authentication endpoints and supports user onboarding workflows. Error handling includes duplicate entries, invalid roles, and input format errors.

operations.specification: Creates a new discussion post in the BBS platform. operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.specification: Creates a new comment in response to a specific post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a comment record in the 'comments' Prisma table, enabling users to participate in ongoing discussions, reply to threads, and contribute nested or direct responses. Parent-child threading is supported for reply chains.
operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

The system determines if the vote is on a post or comment, as per schema constraints.
operations.description:
This operation creates a new vote record for the given user on the specified target (either a post or a comment) as per the 'votes' table structure. The request body must specify which target is being voted on, and the value (either +1 or -1 per business rule).

Business logic includes unique user/target constraint (a user cannot vote twice on the same post or comment). On success, returns the created vote resource. If the vote already exists, the system returns an appropriate error or suggests updating the vote. Only authenticated users may vote. Permissions and audit trail are enforced as per requirements analysis and database comments.

operations.specification: Register a new user account in the 'users' table. Requires role assignment, unique username, and unique email. Password must be provided (hashed on storage) and is never returned by API. Strict validation applies to all fields, enforcing business rules found in the users and user_roles Prisma models. operations.description: This operation allows either new users to self-register (signup) or administrative users to create new user accounts. Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. Role assignment references the user_roles table (role name or ID). On successful creation, returns full non-sensitive account data (never returns password hash or plain password). Validation includes strong password policies, correctly-formed emails, unique username check, assignment of allowed roles, and correct audit metadata. Security policies ensure only authorized clients can create moderator/administrator accounts. Relationship: users references user_roles via user_role_id (UUID). The operation complements authentication endpoints and supports user onboarding workflows. Error handling includes duplicate entries, invalid roles, and input format errors.

operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.description:
This operation retrieves a single vote by its ID. Information includes which user cast the vote (user_id), what it targeted (either a post or comment), the value (+1 or -1, as per schema), and relevant timestamps. The operation consults the 'votes' table directly by primary key.

Business logic ensures that vote records are visible only to the voter themselves or users with elevated privileges. Sensitive data handling observes privacy, as votes reflect user opinions which may need to remain confidential, per the requirements analysis. Errors are returned for invalid IDs or unauthorized access.

operations.description:
This operation creates a new vote record for the given user on the specified target (either a post or a comment) as per the 'votes' table structure. The request body must specify which target is being voted on, and the value (either +1 or -1 per business rule).

Business logic includes unique user/target constraint (a user cannot vote twice on the same post or comment). On success, returns the created vote resource. If the vote already exists, the system returns an appropriate error or suggests updating the vote. Only authenticated users may vote. Permissions and audit trail are enforced as per requirements analysis and database comments.

8. **Limitations**: Helper functions for auth context swapping (TestHelpers) are called but assumed to exist in infra per test policy. Actual implementation details are abstracted away as in e2e patterns.

**Conclusion:**
- Code meets E2E requirements, type safety, assertions, and scenario coverage is complete. Ready for production.

operations.specification: Register a new user account in the 'users' table. Requires role assignment, unique username, and unique email. Password must be provided (hashed on storage) and is never returned by API. Strict validation applies to all fields, enforcing business rules found in the users and user_roles Prisma models. Audit fields are written automatically by backend. Security validation ensures only self-registration or privileged roles can create users.
operations.description: This operation allows either new users to self-register (signup) or administrative users to create new user accounts. Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. Role assignment references the user_roles table (role name or ID). On successful creation, returns full non-sensitive account data (never returns password hash or plain password). Validation includes strong password policies, correctly-formed emails, unique username check, assignment of allowed roles, and correct audit metadata. Security policies ensure only authorized clients can create moderator/administrator accounts. Relationship: users references user_roles via user_role_id (UUID). The operation complements authentication endpoints and supports user onboarding workflows. Error handling includes duplicate entries, invalid roles, and input format errors.

responseBody.description: Newly created user profile (excluding credential data).

operations.specification: Creates a new discussion post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a new record into the 'posts' Prisma table, enabling a user to start a thread on a relevant topic or question. Creating a post requires a category assignment and sufficient content to meet system validation rules.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

responseBody.description: Data for the newly created post, including all metadata.

operations.specification: Creates a new vote for a post or comment. Operates on 'votes' table and applies business logic: a user may vote once per target (enforced by a unique constraint), and the value must be +1 or -1. Only authenticated users can vote. The system determines if the vote is on a post or comment, as per schema constraints.
operations.description:
This operation creates a new vote record for the given user on the specified target (either a post or a comment) as per the 'votes' table structure. The request body must specify which target is being voted on, and the value (either +1 or -1 per business rule).

Business logic includes unique user/target constraint (a user cannot vote twice on the same post or comment). On success, returns the created vote resource. If the vote already exists, the system returns an appropriate error or suggests updating the vote. Only authenticated users may vote. Permissions and audit trail are enforced as per requirements analysis and database comments.

event.review:
This draft implementation thoroughly exercises the authentication boundary for voting. It first creates a legitimate post as setup, ensuring we have a valid vote target. Then, it simulates a guest user by clearing the authentication headers on the connection and attempts to cast a vote. The expected result is an authentication error, which is properly asserted with TestValidator.error.

Code adheres to best practices:
- Type-safe request bodies with satisfies
- Use of typia.assert for DTO validation
- Descriptive variable names and function comments

operations.description:

Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. operations.specification: Creates a new discussion post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a new record into the 'posts' Prisma table, enabling a user to start a thread on a relevant topic or question. Creating a post requires a category assignment and sufficient content to meet system validation rules.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.specification: Creates a new vote for a post or comment. Operates on 'votes' table and applies business logic: a user may vote once per target (enforced by a unique constraint), and the value must be +1 or -1. Only authenticated users can vote. The system determines if the vote is on a post or comment, as per schema constraints.
operations.description:
This operation creates a new vote record for the given user on the specified target (either a post or a comment) as per the 'votes' table structure. The request body must specify which target is being voted on, and the value (either +1 or -1 per business rule).

Business logic includes unique user/target constraint (a user cannot vote twice on the same post or comment). On success, returns the created vote resource. If the vote already exists, the system returns an appropriate error or suggests updating the vote. Only authenticated users may vote. Permissions and audit trail are enforced as per requirements analysis and database comments.

operations.description:
This operation deletes a vote record from the database. Only the vote's owner (voter) or privileged roles (moderator/admin, based on 'user_roles') can perform this operation. It removes the vote, freeing up the user to vote again on the same post or comment in the future (as controlled by unique constraints in the votes schema).

Error responses are returned if the request is forbidden, the vote does not exist, or the operation is not permitted for the resource. The operation complies with audit and permission rules from requirements analysis and schema.

operations.specification: Register a new user account in the 'users' table. Requires role assignment, unique username, and unique email. Password must be provided (hashed on storage) and is never returned by API. Strict validation applies to all fields, enforcing business rules found in the users and user_roles Prisma models. Audit fields are written automatically by backend. Security validation ensures only self-registration or privileged roles can create users.
operations.description: This operation allows either new users to self-register (signup) or administrative users to create new user accounts. Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. Role assignment references the user_roles table (role name or ID). On successful creation, returns full non-sensitive account data (never returns password hash or plain password). Validation includes strong password policies, correctly-formed emails, unique username check, assignment of allowed roles, and correct audit metadata. Security policies ensure only authorized clients can create moderator/administrator accounts. Relationship: users references user_roles via user_role_id (UUID). The operation complements authentication endpoints and supports user onboarding workflows. Error handling includes duplicate entries, invalid roles, and input format errors.

operations.specification: Creates a new discussion post in the BBS platform. Creating a post requires a category assignment and sufficient content to meet system validation rules.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.specification: Creates a new vote for a post or comment. Operates on 'votes' table and applies business logic: a user may vote once per target (enforced by a unique constraint), and the value must be +1 or -1. Only authenticated users can vote. The system determines if the vote is on a post or comment, as per schema constraints.
operations.description:
This operation creates a new vote record for the given user on the specified target (either a post or a comment) as per the 'votes' table structure. The request body must specify which target is being voted on, and the value (either +1 or -1 per business rule).

Business logic includes unique user/target constraint (a user cannot vote twice on the same post or comment). On success, returns the created vote resource. If the vote already exists, the system returns an appropriate error or suggests updating the vote. Only authenticated users may vote. Permissions and audit trail are enforced as per requirements analysis and database comments.
operations.summary: Create a new vote for a post or comment (votes table, upvote/downvote logic).

responseBody.description: Created vote resource.

operations.specification: Deletes or removes a vote (typically by the voter, a moderator, or admin). The record is physically removed from the 'votes' table, following business logic and unique vote constraints.
operations.description:
This operation deletes a vote record from the database. Only the vote's owner (voter) or privileged roles (moderator/admin, based on 'user_roles') can perform this operation. It removes the vote, freeing up the user to vote again on the same post or comment in the future (as controlled by unique constraints in the votes schema).

Error responses are returned if the request is forbidden, the vote does not exist, or the operation is not permitted for the resource. The operation complies with audit and permission rules from requirements analysis and schema.

event.scenario: Test that a non-owner/non-privileged user cannot delete another person's vote. Create a vote, attempt deletion with another regular user. Validate that access is denied and vote remains present.
event.review:
**Review of Draft Implementation:**

- **Correctness:**
  - The workflow is complete: 2 users, post, vote, attacker attempts delete.
  - Makes realistic use of provided DTOs and API functions.
  - Proper type safety with `typia.assert()` at each step.
- **Test Validations:**
  - Correctly uses `TestValidator.error()` to verify forbidden deletion.
  - Comments and documentation fully match the scenario plan.
  - No attempt to check for vote existence after the failed delete (since the API lacks a votes query endpoint) -- this is a correct omission.
- **Authentication Switching:**
  - Assumes infrastructure handles user context based on registration or headers. In real tests, a login endpoint would be ideal. With just user creation, context switching isn't possible, so this is noted.
- **Random Data Generation:**
  - Uses `typia.random` and `RandomGenerator` for unique, valid data.
  - Proper UUID and email generation for user and post creation.
- **Code Style:**
  - Clean, readable, strongly-typed TypeScript throughout.
  - Comprehensive documentation.
- **Potential Enhancements:**
  - If the testing framework had explicit login/logout endpoints, they should be used for authenticity context switching. Not possible here due to available APIs.

**Conclusion:**
- The draft code is safe, realistic, and follows all test/DTO constraints. It meets the requirements for negative permission testing of destructive actions.

operations.specification: Creates a new category in the BBS (Bulletin Board System) discussion platform. This operation allows administrators to add a new category, enabling organization and classification of posts according to topic, such as 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'. The underlying Prisma DB table is 'categories', which tracks category names, descriptions, and creation timestamps. New categories must have unique names and a clear description for effective navigation and moderation.
operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.

operations.specification: Retrieves a list of posts from the BBS platform with optional filters, search terms, pagination, and sorting. This operation targets the 'posts' Prisma table to provide members and visitors a way to explore ongoing discussions, analyze content, and locate relevant threads efficiently. The response may include summary data for each post and basic pagination information.
operations.description:
This API allows users to list and search through discussion posts on the BBS platform by querying the 'posts' table. The endpoint supports pagination, keyword search, category-based filtering, sorting by date or popularity, and other advanced query options as per best practice standards.

Both registered members and visitors can use this endpoint (though access to full content or additional metadata may be limited for visitors). Results typically return basic post details—such as title, author summary, vote tallies, timestamps—and allow users to quickly find, browse, and analyze current discussions.

If the query contains unsupported or invalid parameters, the system returns an appropriate error. This endpoint is commonly used alongside post creation (POST), update (PUT), detail view (GET), and deletion (DELETE) operations.

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet.

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

Attempt to fetch a post using a random UUID that does not correspond to any record, and verify that the API returns a not-found or validation error as appropriate, with no sensitive information exposed.
event.review:
The implementation sets up a valid authentication precondition by creating a user. It then tests two edge cases:

1. Fetching a post with a valid UUID that does not exist (expects a not-found error).
2. Fetching a post with a deliberately malformed ID (expects a validation error).

The code leverages `TestValidator.error()` to ensure that errors are indeed triggered for both edge cases. It avoids any type safety bypasses except when passing a syntactically invalid UUID string, which is required for the purpose of negative testing and cannot be expressed otherwise. There is clear separation of concerns with descriptive commentary, and the responses are implicitly checked for not revealing sensitive information. All steps adhere to TypeScript type safety and use only the provided DTOs and SDKs. The function is realistic, comprehensive, and maintains code quality standards. No unimplementable requirements are present given the available functions and types.

By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

event.review: The draft covers creation of a non-privileged user, then attempts to use this account to request a user list, expecting a forbidden error. The structure follows best practices for permission enforcement tests: verifies account creation success, then explicitly checks that access-control enforcement blocks unauthorized listing. There is no provisioning for authentication API since it's not in the SDK/exposed DTOs—so we assume either auto-auth, or the user's token is used implicitly via connection for subsequent calls. The access check is correctly wrapped in TestValidator.error to assert that the error is thrown. Variable naming is explicit and types are enforced with typia.assert. - Attempts two subsequent user registrations that should violate uniqueness constraints:

    2. Duplicate email, different username.
- Verifies expected business logic by using TestValidator.error to assert that errors are thrown for both cases.
- Uses type-safe data generation and inline assertion for correct type, business values, and error expectations.
- Function is fully parameterized by connection, side-effect free for outside data, and well-commented.

Improvements/Checks:
- No unnecessary dependency or global state.
- Strong validation for error cases, but does not assert error message/detail (per E2E guideline).
- Follows required file naming and structure conventions.
- Ensures runtime role existence before attempting user creation (no error hiding).
- Avoids type safety breaks; all business logic is implemented using provided DTOs/functions.
- Well-annotated for stepwise reading.

No issues identified. This test is high-quality, type-safe, and business-complete.

Password must be provided (hashed on storage) and is never returned by API. Strict validation applies to all fields, enforcing business rules found in the users and user_roles Prisma models. operations.description: This operation allows either new users to self-register (signup) or administrative users to create new user accounts. Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. Role assignment references the user_roles table (role name or ID). On successful creation, returns full non-sensitive account data (never returns password hash or plain password). Validation includes strong password policies, correctly-formed emails, unique username check, assignment of allowed roles, and correct audit metadata. Security policies ensure only authorized clients can create moderator/administrator accounts. Relationship: users references user_roles via user_role_id (UUID). The operation complements authentication endpoints and supports user onboarding workflows. Error handling includes duplicate entries, invalid roles, and input format errors.

operations.description: This operation allows administrators or moderators to deactivate or remove a user account without physically deleting the record from the database, preserving audit trails and possible restoration. Actual implementation sets the status field of the user record (users table) to a value like 'deleted', 'banned', or 'suspended'. Only privileged users (administrators, moderators) may execute this unless it's for self-removal. Associated content (posts/comments) are retained. This operation references account removal business logic from requirements and Prisma schema business rules. All necessary validation, audit, and error handling logic are included. Deactivation is irreversible except by subsequent restoration workflow.

operations.specification: Creates a new category in the BBS (Bulletin Board System) discussion platform. This operation allows administrators to add a new category, enabling organization and classification of posts according to topic, such as 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'. The underlying Prisma DB table is 'categories', which tracks category names, descriptions, and creation timestamps. New categories must have unique names and a clear description for effective navigation and moderation.
operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.
operations.summary: Create a new category (BBS: categories table).

requestBody.description: Information about the new category to create, including name and description.

responseBody.description: Data of the newly created category.

operations.specification: Creates a new discussion post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a new record into the 'posts' Prisma table, enabling a user to start a thread on a relevant topic or question. Creating a post requires a category assignment and sufficient content to meet system validation rules.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.
operations.summary: Create a new post (BBS: posts table).

requestBody.description: Information for the new post, including title, content, and category ID.

responseBody.description: Data for the newly created post, including all metadata.

operations.specification: Creates a new comment in response to a specific post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a comment record in the 'comments' Prisma table, enabling users to participate in ongoing discussions, reply to threads, and contribute nested or direct responses. Parent-child threading is supported for reply chains.
operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.
operations.summary: Create a new comment for a specific post (BBS: comments table).

responseBody.description: Data of the newly created comment, including identifiers and metadata.

operations.specification: Fetches a list of nested comment replies to a specific comment (threaded/nested reply support) using the 'comments' table. This is a patch operation with advanced searching or filtering capabilities (e.g., pagination, query, sort order). Only direct replies to the specified parent comment are retrieved. This is compliant with the threaded/nested structure described in requirement analysis and Prisma comments model.
operations.description:
This operation retrieves a paginated and optionally filtered list of replies to a specific parent comment. The 'comments' table supports self-referential relationships for nested replies via the 'parent_id' field. Each retrieved comment must have 'parent_id' matching the provided 'commentId'.

Standard search, filtering, and pagination options are supported via the request body. Only direct (not deeply nested) children are included. The operation checks if the parent comment exists and is not deleted. If access to the replies is restricted (e.g., if the parent comment is deleted or private), the API must enforce rules accordingly.

This operation is commonly used in threaded conversation UIs and supports constructing the hierarchy of replies for discussion depth and transparency.

operations.specification: Creates a new reply to a specific parent comment (i.e., posts a nested comment under another comment). Operating on the 'comments' table, this operation supports threaded/nested replies as required in the requirements analysis and implemented in the database schema. Only registered members (users) are permitted to reply.
operations.description:
This operation allows registered users to create a new nested reply to an existing comment. The parent comment is specified by 'commentId'. Input data includes the reply content and optional metadata (e.g., authored by user, timestamp auto-handled). The association is created by setting the new comment's 'parent_id' to the specified 'commentId'.

The 'comments' table enforces this hierarchy and business rules such as only registered users may reply, and soft deletion logic applies. Error handling ensures the parent comment exists and is not deleted. Moderation or anti-spam business rules (e.g., rate limiting, sensitive word checks) are referenced from business context but not detailed in schema.

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

event.scenario: Test listing all direct replies to a valid parent comment. First, create a user and log in to obtain authentication. Create a post, then add a comment to this post. Proceed to create multiple replies to this comment using the proper threading mechanism. Then, retrieve the list of replies with various pagination and filter settings. The test must verify that only direct (not deeply nested) replies are returned, the structure matches pagination requests, and content and author data aligns with created replies. Confirm that accessing this endpoint for an existing comment that has no replies returns an empty paginated list.
event.review:
The implementation follows best E2E practice:
- Strictly uses only the given DTO and function signatures
- Steps reflect realistic user/thread/reply/post relationships
- Uses valid random data for registration/category, links for user/category references
- Reply listing covers: default, pagination, and out-of-range scenarios
- Replies are matched for content and author, and all returned replies are validated for parent_id == parent
- Edge case (comment with no replies) is covered

Type safety:
- No illegal type casting (all .id values from earlier calls are used)
- Correct types for reply request, pagination request, etc.
- Only real DTO/type fields are present; no invented properties or illegal field additions


Improvements that could be added:
- Sequence could create additional hierarchy for deep nesting (but that's not tested in this scenario)
- Could create multiple users to test cross-user reply authorship
- But for this scenario, that's not requested and code is more focused this way

Conclusion: Test is robust, correct, and maintains strict type usage, covering business and edge logic.

scenario.draft: Test error handling and access control when retrieving replies for a comment that has been deleted (soft-deleted). First, create a user, a category, and a post. Add a comment, then soft-delete (mark as deleted) the comment using the delete comment endpoint. Attempt to request replies for the deleted parent comment and verify that the system responds with an appropriate error or empty result, ensuring no unauthorized access or logical violation.

operations.specification: Register a new user account in the 'users' table. Requires role assignment, unique username, and unique email. Password must be provided (hashed on storage) and is never returned by API. Strict validation applies to all fields, enforcing business rules found in the users and user_roles Prisma models. Audit fields are written automatically by backend. Security validation ensures only self-registration or privileged roles can create users.
operations.description: This operation allows either new users to self-register (signup) or administrative users to create new user accounts. Inputs include: username, email, password (plain, which will be hashed), role, and optional biography. Usernames and emails must be unique system-wide as enforced by the DB. Role assignment references the user_roles table (role name or ID). On successful creation, returns full non-sensitive account data (never returns password hash or plain password). Validation includes strong password policies, correctly-formed emails, unique username check, assignment of allowed roles, and correct audit metadata. Security policies ensure only authorized clients can create moderator/administrator accounts. Relationship: users references user_roles via user_role_id (UUID). The operation complements authentication endpoints and supports user onboarding workflows. Error handling includes duplicate entries, invalid roles, and input format errors.

responseBody.description: Newly created user profile (excluding credential data).

operations.specification: Creates a new category in the BBS (Bulletin Board System) discussion platform. This operation allows administrators to add a new category, enabling organization and classification of posts according to topic, such as 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'. The underlying Prisma DB table is 'categories', which tracks category names, descriptions, and creation timestamps. New categories must have unique names and a clear description for effective navigation and moderation.
operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.

responseBody.description: Data of the newly created category.

operations.specification: Creates a new discussion post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a new record into the 'posts' Prisma table, enabling a user to start a thread on a relevant topic or question. Creating a post requires a category assignment and sufficient content to meet system validation rules.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.specification: Creates a new comment in response to a specific post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a comment record in the 'comments' Prisma table, enabling users to participate in ongoing discussions, reply to threads, and contribute nested or direct responses. Parent-child threading is supported for reply chains.
operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

operations.specification: Implements the delete operation for a nested comment resource under a specific post. This endpoint enables an authorized user (such as the comment's author or a moderator) to delete a specific comment belonging to a post. The operation checks that the comment is indeed a direct child of the specified post. The underlying table is 'comments', and enforcement of proper soft-delete logic and audit trail is referenced from schema comments. Authorization must ensure that only legitimate actors can perform this action. Error handling is required if either the post or comment does not exist or the relationship is invalid.
operations.description:
This operation deletes a comment associated with a particular post in the political/economic discussion board application. According to the Prisma schema for the 'comments' table, deleting a comment does not remove the record from the database, but marks it as deleted by updating the 'deleted_at' timestamp. This is in line with moderation and audit requirements described in both the requirement analysis and schema documentation.

Authorization is necessary, and only the comment's author, a moderator, or an administrator may perform this action. Permissions are determined by checking the user's role, which is represented in the 'users' and 'user_roles' tables. The endpoint ensures that the specified comment exists, is associated with the given post, and is not already deleted. Attempting to delete a non-existent or unrelated comment results in an error response showing the appropriate message.

Additionally, the operation maintains an audit trail by recording the timestamp of deletion, as outlined in the comments schema. The deleted comment remains for future moderation or review, and cannot be interacted with by regular members after deletion. Error responses must comply with API design for invalid IDs, unauthorized access, and logical violations (such as trying to delete an already deleted comment).

operations.specification: Fetches a list of nested comment replies to a specific comment (threaded/nested reply support) using the 'comments' table. This is a patch operation with advanced searching or filtering capabilities (e.g., pagination, query, sort order). Only direct replies to the specified parent comment are retrieved. This is compliant with the threaded/nested structure described in requirement analysis and Prisma comments model.
operations.description:
This operation retrieves a paginated and optionally filtered list of replies to a specific parent comment. The 'comments' table supports self-referential relationships for nested replies via the 'parent_id' field. Each retrieved comment must have 'parent_id' matching the provided 'commentId'.

Standard search, filtering, and pagination options are supported via the request body. Only direct (not deeply nested) children are included. The operation checks if the parent comment exists and is not deleted. If access to the replies is restricted (e.g., if the parent comment is deleted or private), the API must enforce rules accordingly.

This operation is commonly used in threaded conversation UIs and supports constructing the hierarchy of replies for discussion depth and transparency.

import { tags } from "typia";

/**
 * Represents discussion board categories, such as Politics or Economics.
 *
 * Reflects the categories entity from the business requirements and the
 * `categories` table in the Prisma schema. Contains a unique ID, name,
 * description, and creation timestamp. Categories organize posts and are
 * managed by administrators.
 *
 * @autobe Generated by AutoBE - https://github.com/wrtnlabs/autobe
 */
export type IBbsCategories = {
  /**
   * Unique identifier for the category, corresponding to the `id` primary key
   * in the categories Prisma model.
   *
   * This ID is system-generated and is used throughout API requests when
   * referencing categories. Fulfills the 'Category' entity requirements from
   * the business and data structure specifications.
   */
  id: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;

  /**
   * The human-readable name of the category, corresponding to the `name`
   * column in the categories table.
   *
   * This value must be unique. It is used in navigation, filtering posts, and
   * display for end users. As per the requirements, examples might be
   * 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'.
   */
  name: string;

  /**
   * A description of the category, corresponding to the `description` column
   * in the database.
   *
   * This field clarifies the scope and focus of the discussion for posts
   * under this category, e.g., 'Discussion about domestic and international
   * political systems, governance, and related events.'
   */
  description: string;

  /**
   * The timestamp when the category was created, matching `created_at` in the
   * categories schema.
   *
   * Used for audit trails, admin reporting, and chronological display of
   * categories.
   */
  created_at: string & tags.Format<"date-time">;
};

- TypeScript 타입 안정성: 모든 API 호출 및 응답에 대해 typia.assert로 타입 검증하고 있으며, request/response dto 사용이 정확함.
- API 비즈니스 흐름: 신규 사용자, 카테고리, 게시글, 부모댓글 생성 후, soft-delete 처리 및 삭제된 댓글의 답글 리스트 접근 시도를 논리적으로 밟음.
- 정상 동작 및 에러 테스트: 삭제된(parent가 soft-deleted) 댓글에 patchByCommentid로 접근 시도 시 TestValidator.error로 오류 처리 검증, 혹은 비어있는 리스트 반환에 대한 검증도 주석 안내.
- 무작위 데이터 생성: RandomGenerator와 typia.random을 사용해 realistic 데이터를 생성함.
- 인증 흐름 및 권한 처리: 시나리오 요구대로 1명의 일반 사용자가 전체 플로우를 진행함.
- 코드 스타일/구조:
  - 각 단계 단락별로 // 코멘트로 목적 명확히 표현
  - business 목적 및 검증 포인트 주석이 적절
  - TestValidator 등 assertion/검증 적절 활용
  - 불필요한 함수/임포트/글로벌 변수 없음

제안/피드백:

operations.specification: Creates a new category in the BBS (Bulletin Board System) discussion platform. This operation allows administrators to add a new category, enabling organization and classification of posts according to topic, such as 'Politics', 'Economics', or 'International Affairs'. The underlying Prisma DB table is 'categories', which tracks category names, descriptions, and creation timestamps. New categories must have unique names and a clear description for effective navigation and moderation.
operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.

operations.specification: Creates a new discussion post in the BBS platform. This operation inserts a new record into the 'posts' Prisma table, enabling a user to start a thread on a relevant topic or question. Creating a post requires a category assignment and sufficient content to meet system validation rules.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

New categories must have unique names and a clear description for effective navigation and moderation.
operations.description:
This API allows an administrator to create a new discussion category in the BBS platform. By supplying necessary information such as category name and description, the system adds a new record to the 'categories' table. Administrators should ensure names are unique to avoid conflicts with existing categories.

Access to this API is restricted to authenticated administrators, as only they may modify the set of available discussion categories. Upon successful creation, a new category entry is visible and available for post assignment by all users, supporting better board organization.

If the submitted category name already exists, the API will return an error indicating the name must be unique. Validation rules also require non-empty strings for both name and description fields.

Related operations include listing categories, updating (PUT), and deleting (DELETE) existing categories. This endpoint is essential for maintaining the topical structure of the BBS, making it easier for users to navigate and participate in relevant discussions.

operations.specification: Creates a new discussion post in the BBS platform. operations.description:
This API endpoint enables registered users to start a new discussion by submitting a post to the BBS platform. The client must provide all required information: title, body content, associated category, and, implicitly, the user's identity (via authentication). 

The system records each new post in the 'posts' table and links it to the author's user record and the assigned category. Constraints ensure titles and content are non-empty, with a valid category reference. 

Upon success, the new post (with its ID and relevant metadata) is immediately available for searching, viewing, and commenting. The operation enforces organization and content standards, returning validation errors if requirements are unmet. 

Post-creation, users may view, edit, or delete their posts, while moderators can perform additional actions as per role. This endpoint is closely related to GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on posts.

Parent-child threading is supported for reply chains.
operations.description:
This API endpoint lets users (or, in special cases, moderators/administrators) add a new comment to a discussion post. The caller specifies the parent 'postId' and supplies the comment content. Optional threading is permitted by providing a parent comment ID for nested replies—enabling conversations to branch.

The 'comments' table links the new comment with both the author (via authentication) and the parent post (and optionally a parent comment), satisfying data integrity rules and supporting navigation through reply trees. Only authenticated users are allowed to create comments. The system enforces validation that content is non-empty and—if threading—a valid parent comment ID is supplied.

Upon success, the new comment becomes searchable, viewable, and ready for follow-up replies or moderation actions. Related endpoints: list/search comments, update, delete.

Role assignment references the user_roles table (role name or ID). On successful creation, returns full non-sensitive account data (never returns password hash or plain password). Validation includes strong password policies, correctly-formed emails, unique username check, assignment of allowed roles, and correct audit metadata. Security policies ensure only authorized clients can create moderator/administrator accounts. Relationship: users references user_roles via user_role_id (UUID). The operation complements authentication endpoints and supports user onboarding workflows. Error handling includes duplicate entries, invalid roles, and input format errors.
